text:
marco: Hey — quick question. I opened a PR that touches runtime/service-a, api/handlers, and docs/upgrade. CODEOWNERS has @runtime-team for runtime/, @api-team for api/, and @docs for docs/. Who can actually approve/merge here? do I need all three approvals?
angela: short answer: yes if we follow CODEOWNERS strictly. long answer: depends on scope of changes and whether it's just doc churn.
ryan: If the runtime change is non-trivial (behavioral) we need a runtime owner sign-off. API changes likewise. Docs-only updates can usually be OK with a @docs approval, but combined changes escalate.
sam: Also watch CI: our branch protection requires 1 codeowner approval OR an override from an approver listed in the repo's OWNERS.md (team leads). If it's touching multiple owners, GitHub requires approvals from each matching CODEOWNERS path.
marco: Okay — this is a small bugfix in runtime caching behavior plus a docs clarification. The runtime change updates a single line in runtime/cache.cpp and adds a note in docs/upgrade.md. Does that still need full set?
angela: If runtime code changes behavior, runtime must review. Docs alone wouldn't cover it. If you can split into two PRs (runtime + docs), that's best: runtime PR gets runtime owners, docs PR can be docs-only and merged faster.
ryan: FWIW, here's what CODEOWNERS looks like in this repo right now:
```text
# CODEOWNERS
/runtime/ @runtime-team
/api/ @api-team
/docs/ @docs
```
so github will request reviews from each matched owner.
sam: There's also an internal fallback: repo-admins (listed in OWNERS.md) can approve a multi-owner PR if they confirm all teams are okay. That requires a short note in the PR describing why it's safe and an explicit admin approval. Not ideal for routine changes.
marco: Would tagging @runtime-team and @docs with a summary be enough to avoid blocking? I'll ping them.
angela: Yes do that. Add a short checklist in the PR: what changed, why safe, test results. If runtime owner marks as "approved" and docs approves, you can merge once CI passes. If api owners aren't required (no API code changed) you won't need them.
ryan: Also option: request a codeowners exemption label (label: codeowners-exempt) but that's restricted to Security/PM/product-approved infra churn and requires eng lead sign-off. Don't use that for normal fixes.
marco: noted. I'll split into two PRs if the runtime diff grows; for now I'll ping runtime + docs and add test logs. thanks.
pr-bot: PR #4821 opened by marco: runtime: fix cache invalidation; docs: add upgrade note — checks: pending / required reviews: @runtime-team, @docs
sam: follow-up: if you need faster merge and runtime owner is slow, ping a runtime lead directly or add a "needs-owner" label so oncall sees it. but respect the review process.
marco: will do — pinging now. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
